nodes.summary: Win probability of a threshold rule in the random-order model (Ferguson, *Optimal Stopping and Applications*, Chapter 2, equation (3)). For `1 ≤ r ≤ n`, the rule `N_r` rejects the applicants interviewed at times `0, …, r - 2` and selects the first later applicant who is best so far. The proportion of permutations for which the selected applicant is the best of all equals `winProb n r`.

nodes.summary: The `1/e` law of the secretary problem (Ferguson, *Optimal Stopping and Applications*, Chapter 2, end of §2.1): the win probability of the optimal threshold rule tends to `1/e`, `P_{r₁(n)} → 1/e` as `n → ∞`.
nodes.title: The `1/e` law of the secretary problem

nodes.summary: The optimal threshold rule of the secretary problem (Ferguson, *Optimal Stopping and Applications*, Chapter 2, equation (4)): for `n ≥ 1`, the threshold `r₁ = min {r ≥ 1 : ∑_{k=r+1}^{n} 1/(k - 1) ≤ 1}` maximises the win probability `P_r` of the threshold rules `N_r` over `1 ≤ r ≤ n`.
nodes.title: The optimal threshold rule of the secretary problem

nodes.summary: Increment of the win probability of threshold rules (Ferguson, *Optimal Stopping and Applications*, Chapter 2, the computation before equation (4)): for `1 ≤ r < n`, `P_{r+1} - P_r = (T_r - 1)/n`, so `P_{r+1} ≤ P_r` if and only if `∑_{k=r+1}^{n} 1/(k - 1) ≤ 1`.
nodes.title: Increment of the win probability of threshold rules

nodes.summary: For `n` applicants and threshold `r ≥ 1`, `P_r = (1 + (r - 1) T_r)/n` with `T_r = ∑_{j=r}^{n-1} 1/j`; this is Ferguson's equation (3), `P_r = ((r - 1)/n) ∑_{k=r}^{n} 1/(k - 1)` for `r ≥ 2` and `P_1 = 1/n` (*Optimal Stopping and Applications*, Chapter 2, §2.1).
